title: Forgiving family
hookLine: the one who keeps ties isn't the one who repays, but the one who reconnects when cut off (Bukhari)
tomorrow: Jordan's whole family is coming to dinner. what does Dadi make first?

lines: NOT THE ONE WHO PAYS BACK.
THE ONE WHO JOINS IT AGAIN.
cards: He cut me off first. Every family silence has that sentence somewhere inside it, and it isn't even wrong. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari answers it head-on.
The Prophet ﷺ said: the one who keeps family ties, al-wasil, isn't the one who pays back in kind. It's the one who, when the tie is cut, joins it again. So who's right?
The hadith doesn't say the one who cut was right. It says who the keeper is.

teach.b: Now two voices, and both come from the sources. The first says: fairness is allowed.

teach.h: PARDON, AND THE REWARD IS GOD'S.
teach.b: The Qur'an itself says the recompense for a wrong is a wrong like it, and that whoever pardons and makes peace, their reward is with God. Notice the first half is permitted. Waiting for an apology isn't a sin.
Someone who was truly wronged doesn't owe anyone a show of being fine. The second voice says: yes, but look where the reward sits. In Sahih Muslim, a man tells the Prophet: I have relatives.
I keep the ties; they cut them. I'm good to them; they're bad to me.

The Prophet answers: if it is as you say, it's as if you were feeding them hot ashes, and a helper from God will stay with you as long as you keep it up. The keeper isn't the one who wins the argument.
It's the one who calls again. Both voices are in the text, and neither cancels the other. One protects the person who was hurt.
The other points them toward the door anyway.
And one line that matters: this is about cold silences, not danger.
Nobody is asked to walk back into harm. One to tell a friend tonight: in the hadith, the keeper of the tie is defined by what they do after it's cut.

how: Muslims treat cutting off kin as a serious wrong; after a quarrel, the hadith praises whichever of the two greets the other first.

o: a yearly gathering where families settle old fights
letting a relative's wrong go without mentioning it
joining a family tie again after someone cut it

games.q: what goes with what — tap the pairs.
p: the one who joins it again
pardon, and the reward is God's
stays while you keep it up

s: in the hadith, the keeper of ties is the one who repays kindness with kindness
that's paying back in kind; the keeper joins the tie again when it's cut.
the Qur'an allows a response equal to a wrong, and praises pardon
42:40: whoever pardons and makes peace, their reward is with God.
reconnecting means putting yourself back in harm's way
the lesson is about cold silences, not danger.

games.q: your cousin says reaching out to an aunt who insulted her mom would be fake. before you answer, what's the strongest case for her side?
o: the Qur'an allows a fair response to a wrong, so waiting for an apology isn't a sin.
the hadith says family ties only count when both sides keep them.
forgiving family is only required once the other person asks for it.
games.why: her best case is the first half of 42:40: a fair response is allowed. the other side adds the second half, and the hadith: the keeper is the one who reconnects.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind someone in your family the tie has gone cold with, or someone you've gone quiet on. Don't plan a speech.
Picture only the first small step that would join it again, a greeting, a 'thinking of you', and notice what your chest does as you picture it.

wordCard.voice: Forgiving family: being the one who joins the tie again after it's cut, not only the one who pays back in kind.

orig.note: Arabic: the one who joins; the keeper of ties in Bukhari 5991.

carryVoice: Carry this one word: reconnect, even when they cut it first. Seven of ten, and the hardest.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 5991 (the keeper of ties is not the one who repays in kind, but the one who joins them when they are cut)
Qur'an 42:40 (the recompense of a wrong is a wrong like it; whoever pardons and makes peace, his reward is with God)
Sahih Muslim 2558 (relatives who cut him off: as if feeding them hot ashes; a helper from God stays with him)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6077 (after a quarrel, the better of the two is the one who greets first)
